segments.text: The world population has passed 8 billion
Yet more than 800 million people still lack enough food and suffer from hunger
Agriculture is one of the oldest industries of humanity
And the foundation of civilization
Since the invention of irrigation, farming in ancient Mesopotamia, humanity has multiplied
crop yields many times over through improved varieties and new technology.
In the green revolution of the 20th century, high yield varieties and chemical fertilizers
Fertilizers dramatically increased food production in Asia and Africa
But at the same time, the excessive use of pesticides and fertilizers has contaminated soil and water
Causing long-term problems in recent years
Both organic farming and genetically modified crops have drawn attention
The former is kinder to the environment, but difficult for mass production
The latter raises yields, but leaves concerns about safety
Another major problem is food waste in developed countries
About one third of all food produced is thrown away
In a world where people go hungry, this is a serious contradiction
Solving the food problem requires more than increasing production
Improvement in distribution, reduction of waste
And a change in the awareness of each consumer are all needed
To feed the world in a sustainable way
Is the greatest challenge of the coming century
